ask: Design the /roadmap skill: what it reads in a repo, how the page is laid out, and how merges update a step's status.
note: Shows, per repo: every debt and note, your feedback items and where each went, the repo's plans, each session's own plan, and open PRs and branches. Accuracy rule: the page reads each item from its one home and stores no copy, shows when it last read, and marks anything it could not read as unknown. Needs fb items homed in the repo first. Session pages (live) sit under this repo page (lasting). Your idea, Oct 22: a far better live view, with pixel-art workers that move and show what each one is doing (building, reviewing, waiting on CI, waiting on you, done). Limits from c26 (watching costs less than what it watches): the view draws from records sessions already write, read when the page is open; no new watcher, timer or log. Where each worker's live state comes from is still open; the design pass names it. Your rule, Oct 21: the page is a current record, not a log. Each filing rewrites the note it touches to the current state (a ruling stays as one dated line), merges a new item into an existing step when they overlap, and fixes the order. A review pass now and then checks the whole page for overlaps, stale dependencies and drift from the repo. Proof it is needed: this page grew add-only for four days until a cleanup pass on Oct 21. Also from Oct 21: one view per phase with its four key numbers, steps folded to their titles, done steps struck through. Your pick: B, logbook (claude.ai/artifact/9H4NgQdoNNhU939mXojVv9), and you have started UI changes to it (you, Oct 22). A, glance board, and C, notebook, are not used. Each themes per repo from one block of tokens.
title: Give every repo a living roadmap page
why: The process behind this page, made repeatable: audit the repo, turn the findings into phased steps with a plain why and an ask for each, publish one page per repo, and update it in place as lanes land. A /roadmap skill in claude-settings would build it from docs/plans and docs/debts, and the merge step would tick off the steps it completes. It pairs with the health view: health shows how the repo is, the roadmap shows what's next.
